title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
Scammers used AI-generated videos and deepfakes to impersonate a real immigration attorney on social media, creating hundreds of fake profiles offering legal services the attorney does not provide. The system deployed was generative video technology capable of producing convincing likenesses, combined with social media platforms that did not prevent the creation or spread of impersonation content at scale. Catching this would have required either social media platforms to verify the identity of accounts offering professional services before amplification, or to detect and remove AI-generated impersonations faster than the six to twelve weeks it reportedly took after the scheme began.

The failure occurred at the deployment stage of both the generative AI technology and the social media platforms hosting it. Scammers had no technical barrier to creating deepfakes or fake profiles, and social media did not implement checks sufficient to stop the spread before victims lost money. It is not established whether the AI video generation tool was built with safeguards against impersonation, or whether the platform operators knew of the scheme before the attorney's team hired external investigators.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of an artificial intelligence scam targeting vulnerable immigrants. Criminals have created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos featuring Leal offering immigration services he never provides, including US residency assistance for $2,200. The scheme began escalating dramatically about three months ago after potential clients started calling his office about the fraudulent offers. Leal's team hired an anti-piracy company that has removed nearly 6,500 fake accounts, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram.

The scammers typically use social media videos directing viewers to contact phone numbers via WhatsApp, then exchange emails with fake contracts. Some videos feature AI-generated testimonials from supposed former clients praising Leal's services. Leal warns consumers to be cautious of requests for payment through Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App, and emphasizes his office never requests payment over the phone. He has changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate the fraud's origin while urging immigrants to verify the identity of anyone offering legal services online.
